result_text:
Any folder whose name starts with `mock` or `__mock` now counts as a mock-resources folder, whatever follows in the name. The new test passes; I only ran that one class, not the rest of the `codeanalyzer` tests.

- **Fix:** In `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventions.java` (around line 393), the two mock rules required at least one ASCII letter, digit, `_`, `-` or space after `mock`/`__mock`. They now accept any run of characters except `/` and `\`: `.*/__mock[^/\\]*/.*` and `.*/mock[^/\\]*/.*`. That covers plain `mock`, `mock.data`, `mock(old)`, `mock-größe` and `mock模拟`.
- **Same-folder match:** The match stays inside one folder name, because the `mock` must follow a `/` and the characters after it can't include a slash.
- **Backslash paths:** These already work, since `SourceFileFilter` also tries a slash-normalised copy of the path.
- **Test:** I added `codeanalyzer/src/test/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/MockFolderConventionTest.java`.
  - It checks that `mock`, `mocks`, `__mocks__`, `mock-data`, `mock_data`, `mock data`, `mockStore`, the new punctuation and non-ASCII names, and `__mock` are all test code, with both `/` and `\` separators.
  - It also checks that `remock/`, `demo/`, `src/main/java/`, `mock.java` and `mockery.java` are not.
